text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "I can claim that Croat officials from Bosnia's Moslem- Croat Federation are not mixed up in the incident but local powerful persons from that part of town," Moslem chairman of the collective Bosnian Presidency Alija Izetbegovic says after Bosnian Croat's attack Moslem pilgrimers in Croat controlled west part of the bitterly divided town of Mostar in which one man was killed and 22 were wounded.

- Continued media campaign and weeks-long armed incidents, in spite of appeals for tensions to calm down, have unfortunately resulted in the bloody confrontation on the streets of Mostar, Croat member in the Bosnian collective Presidency Kresimir Zubak says in a statement issued after the incident in Mostar.
- Shooting at unarmed civilians is shooting at Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federations, federal prime minister Edhem Bicakcic says in a comment of the Mostar incident.

- Regardless of the outcome of the disputed northern Bosnian town of Brcko arbitration, the office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is urging the authorities and individuals in both Bosnian Serb Republic and Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation to remain calm and to show particular respect for human rights and minority rights during this time, Carrol Faubert, UNHCR special envoy for former Yugoslavia says in a statement. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
